rules.name: follows a primary pointer drag with the slides
rules.source: Carousel.svelte (onpointerdown, onpointermove, drive) and carousel.ts (carouselStep, carouselOffset)
rules.note: The shift is the travel in px toward a side that holds a neighbour, clamped to the carousel width plus the gap; toward a missing neighbour it is resisted (carousel.ts). With prefers-reduced-motion the shift stays 0px. A mouse drags only with button 0, only primary pointers count, and the carousel captures the pointer. Every slot carries the same shift.

rules.name: settles toward the neighbour after a far drag or a flick and then reports the side
rules.source: Carousel.svelte (onpointerup, settled, finish) and carousel.ts (swipeRelease, isFlick)
rules.note: A release reveals a side when the travel is at least 25% of the carousel width or is a flick (at least 24px at 0.4px/ms or faster); a travel of 120px is at least 25% of any carousel up to 480px wide. While settling every slot has is-settling and its shift animates toward the neighbour; the transform transitionend on a slot (or a fallback timer from its transition duration plus 220ms) finishes it. The side is +1 or -1 in screen terms adjusted for dir. The app is expected to replace the slides on onsettled.

rules.name: settles back without reporting after a short drag or a cancelled pointer
rules.source: Carousel.svelte (onpointercancel, onpointerup, settled, finish) and carousel.ts (carouselStep, settleFrom)
rules.note: A cancelled pointer settles back whatever its travel, and so does a release that is neither far nor a flick. The shift animates back to 0px through is-settling like a settle toward a side, and onsettled is not called.

rules.name: ignores the pointer when it is driven
rules.note: A driven carousel moves only through its drive() and finish() methods, called by the app.
